id_and_class.summary: Delaflor's Model Dependent Ontology (MDO) refuses to commit to any substrate, material, mental, or otherwise, and treats theories of consciousness as useful maps rather than discoveries of what experience is. What we call consciousness is ‘C2’, the language-driven organization in which self and world are drawn as paired, practical distinctions; beneath it lies ‘C1’, non-egoic raw experience, and beyond that an undecidable limit that can only be pointed at. Delaflor offers the framework less as a rival theory than as a device, like an extended Zen koan, for clearing the ground every theory stands on.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as a Language-Rendered Model of Self and World

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Conventional consciousness is C2, the focused, intentional, propositional organization that arises when language extends C1, raw non-egoic experience. In C2, experience is rendered as language, self, and world, and the world is part of what C2 renders, not something outside it.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Delaflor sets the mind-body question aside: mind, brain, self, and world are demarcations drawn within experience for practical purposes, operative but ontologically empty. MDO rejects physicalism, idealism, panpsychism, illusionism, transcendental phenomenology, Advaita non-dual idealism, and mysterianism alike.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (MDO denies that consciousness is the primitive and makes no claim about any substrate it could emerge from; the undecidable, C1, and C2 are modes of one continuous operation, not layers)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Self and world arise together as distinctions produced by language use, with neither prior to the other. Intentionality belongs to C2, which is always about a subject and an object; C1 has no ego and no subject-object split.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Raw experience (C1) is treated as a limit condition reached from within, not denied and not explained. Every attempt to derive or reduce it already takes place inside it.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Deliberately minimal: an ongoing encounter between goals and a field of possibilities and constraints. Delaflor treats even these terms as metaphorical handles, not names for an essence.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Neuroscience, phenomenology, anesthesia research, psychiatry, and contemplative practice all produce legitimate maps of how experience varies, judged by whether they predict, intervene, or stabilize. The error is inflating these maps into claims about what experience is.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Three modes of one operation: the undecidable (unnameable, the frontier where the decidable gives out), C1 (non-egoic, operational awareness, as when a driver arrives home with no memory of the route), and C2 (language-structured consciousness with a self-world axis).

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (as limit condition), Self, Intentionality, Intersubjectivity, Machine consciousness
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Language acting as C1's intentional extension produces C2 and, with it, the apparent split between self and world.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: C2 arises whenever language operates on C1; the self-world division is continually generated, not a fixed structure.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: The divisions C2 draws are pragmatic: they serve goals within a field of possibilities and constraints.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: C1 already works as a map of possibilities and constraints, though no one organizes it. The ‘objective world’ arises through inter-objectivity, when overlapping goals coordinate individual maps closely enough for joint action.
core_claims_and_evidence: Every derivation of consciousness takes place within what can be decided, so the undecidable limit can only be pointed at, never grounded or reduced.
A shared world emerges from coordinated maps, which accounts for the absence of a private language without positing a world separate from experiencers; its patterns still resist individual will.

Large language models are stateless events that mimic C2 surface structures without the continuous C1 availability beneath them, so they call for a framework of Artificial Cognition, not artificial consciousness.
A science of consciousness should model how experience varies, not try to discover what experience ultimately is.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical (epistemology and philosophy of science), with contemplative traditions cited as historical echoes, not as support

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Calling C1 ‘non-egoic awareness’ and ‘raw experience’ while denying that it is a ground risks reintroducing the experiential primitive MDO disowns. A framework that declines every ontological position is hard to test or refute.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Delaflor leaves open whether there is any ultimate essence of consciousness to discern or whether the question itself is misguided.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Internally consistent as a meta-framework that brackets ontology, though its explicit rejection of every listed position means it offers no account of what experience is.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Delaflor argues that current language models only mimic C2 structures and lack continuous C1 availability. He treats them as artificial cognition, not consciousness.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: MDO points to an undecidable limit that cannot be named and makes no claim about ultimate purpose.

related_theories.name: Nāgārjuna’s Empty Consciousness: Experience Without Essence
